full_text:
Let me search for the specific long-range paper.**Verdict: KNOWN-VARIANT, with a live dispute over the marginal case. Confidence: medium.**

**1. Model family.** This is the classical 2D XY (planar rotor) model with algebraic long-range couplings, J(r) ∼ 1/r^(2+σ). The 1/r⁴ coupling is σ = 2, which is the marginal case where the long-range and short-range spin-wave terms are degenerate. It sits in statistical physics, in the BKT / Mermin–Wagner / long-range O(2) literature. The simulation uses Wolff-type cluster updates, which is the standard method here.

**2. What the literature says.**
- **Rigorous no-order result.** Bruno (2001) strengthened the Mermin–Wagner theorem. For monotonically decreasing interactions, ferro- or antiferromagnetic long-range order at T>0 is ruled out if α ≥ 2D. In D = 2 and α = 4 this applies to your system. So there is no true long-range order, and m² must go to zero as L→∞. (Bruno, PRL 87, 137203, 2001.)
- **Field-theory phase diagram.** Giachetti, Defenu, Ruffo & Trombettoni (PRL 127, 156801, 2021) treat couplings ∼ r^(−2−σ) in the BKT problem. They find a quasiordered phase in a finite temperature range for 7/4<σ<2. A follow-up is Giachetti, Trombettoni, Ruffo & Defenu, PRB 106, 014106 (2022). These papers concern σ < 2 and the BKT-versus-ordered structure. I did not find in them an explicit σ = 2 prediction of m² ∼ (ln L)^(−cT).
- **Closest Monte Carlo work.** Xiao, Yao, Zhang, Fan & Deng published Chin. Phys. Lett. 42, 070002 (2025). Yao, Xiao, Zhang, Deng & Fan published PRB 112, 144429 (2025), arXiv:2411.01811. They claim that for σ ≤ 2 the system has a second-order transition into a ferromagnetic phase with long-range order. They also claim the correlation function saturates to a nonzero constant as the inverse logarithm of distance for σ = 2. A 2025 Heisenberg follow-up (Xiao et al.), which I read only through a third-party summary, makes the same claim for the marginal point.
- **The dispute.** Your result is a power of ln L with an exponent proportional to T, so m² → 0 slowly. That is the opposite of the Deng-group claim of a finite m² at σ = 2. It agrees with the Bruno bound and with the simple Gaussian spin-wave argument: the stiffness is ∝ ln(1/k), so ⟨θ²⟩ ∼ (T/2πJ) ln ln L and m² ∼ (ln L)^(−T/2πJ).
- **Support for the spin-wave picture.** This is my own derivation, not a source I found. It explains your numbers: the exponent scales with T, and 2π × slope × exponent = 1 is the spin-wave consistency check.

**3. Citation check.** I verified all of the above against search results (titles, authors, venues, years). I did not find an explicit earlier paper stating the (ln L)^(−cT) law at σ = 2, so the ln ln L spin-wave result rests on my derivation plus Bruno's bound.

**4. Possible differences from the literature.**
- **Exponent at β = 8.** The ratio 0.34/0.02 = 17 is not the 8 you would expect from exact proportionality to T. Check this, since 0.02 is a small number and probably noisy.
- **Divergence exponent 2.24.** I found no source for this. The standard BKT form is exp(c/√(T/T_c − 1)), and a power-law fit may be mimicking it. I also did not search for the BKT-to-disordered transition at σ = 2 separately.
- **Nearest-neighbour 1.2 plus weak 1/r⁴ tail.** I did not search for this variant. It is probably covered by the same marginal argument.
